subject: Food Science
title: Saturated vs. Unsaturated
description: Learn Saturated vs. Unsaturated in one minute.

hook.text: Butter is solid at room temperature. Olive oil is liquid. The difference is just a few missing hydrogen atoms.

buildup.text: Saturated fats have no double bonds—their carbon chains pack tightly together, forming solids.

discovery.text: Unsaturated fats have double bonds that create kinks in the chain, preventing tight packing. They stay liquid.

twist.text: Coconut oil is a plant fat but highly saturated—that's why it's solid at room temperature like butter.

climax.text: The number and position of double bonds determines melting point, shelf life, and health effects.

punchline.text: Solid or liquid? It all comes down to kinks in the chain.

quiz.question: Why are unsaturated fats liquid at room temperature?
options: Double bonds create kinks that prevent tight packing
